scope: Kayenta Obsession second-edition base/core; standard 16-round, 2–4-player multiplayer; base objective deck; no marked expansion content, optional modules, variants or alternate modes.
conclusion: I found no material factual contradiction in the 60 keyed answers and no additional question that survives the requested distinct-rule/outcome-branch standard. This is a bounded conclusion for the specified base scope, not a claim that every tile recipe or printed value is separately tested. Several candidate additions were actively considered and rejected below.

source_coverage.scope_result: Seasonal refresh player-aid clarification is relevant and reflected. Solo, hall-boy, Lady Mary and Business Room corrections are outside this base scope.

factual_key_findings.question: Q03/Q07
factual_key_findings.finding: The base-only pass benefits are £200 or Market refresh. Butler’s Room remains an activity in this scope. The expansion/optional hiring-on-pass FAQ must not be imported into the base procedure.
source_refs: Compendium p.21, Hiring When Passing, lines 826–830

factual_key_findings.question: Q04/Q06/Q34
factual_key_findings.finding: The key distinguishes spending reputation as an affordable cost from ignoring excess mandatory loss at the floor. Screening reputation is fixed after step 2, so later special-action losses do not invalidate the activity or guests.

factual_key_findings.question: Q09
factual_key_findings.finding: Butler’s Pantry is the exclusive base route to an underbutler and places him in Expended Service. The key’s ordinary two-rotation delay and separately identified refresh routes follow the service procedures.

factual_key_findings.question: Q12
factual_key_findings.finding: Seasonal full refresh is now the default after the first three courtships. This is not an excluded optional variant under the controlling compendium and corrigendum.
source_refs: Compendium p.23, End of Season and Designer’s Note, lines 884–920
Corrigendum p.2, Player Aid Note, lines 4569–4572

factual_key_findings.question: Q14/Q15
factual_key_findings.finding: The final courtship uses all revealed categories and a reputation-level tiebreak; overall victory first checks the final Fairchild, then reputation level. Wheel position is excluded from these tiebreaks.

factual_key_findings.question: Q20
factual_key_findings.finding: The three suites have materially different selection, service and doubling rules. Queen’s Suite and Lionheart Suite become monuments; Heritage stays an activity. The key preserves these differences.

factual_key_findings.question: Q51/Q52/Q54
factual_key_findings.finding: Base objective wording is used rather than replacement-deck rates. Common-servant objective excludes unique servants; ordinary service VP includes them. Category objectives include monuments and the face-up hybrid category. Guests exclude family and include the final Fairchild.

factual_key_findings.question: Q55
factual_key_findings.finding: The French publisher’s example says maximum reputation level and identifies the Max counter. Together with its standard-game counter description, this supports level 7 rather than requiring wheel position 5. Compendium ordinary reputation VP and tiebreaks also disregard wheel position. Wealth is at least £1200.
source_refs: Authorized French base rulebook p.7, Max counter equals 7 in standard play
Authorized French base rulebook p.14, objective scoring example: maximum reputation level indicated by Max counter

factual_key_findings.question: Q56
factual_key_findings.finding: The key uses the standard activity West Terrace and does not import the alternate ongoing back side.

candidate_rejections.candidate: Separate questions for each remaining base group-objective recipe or servant threshold.
candidate_rejections.reason: These substitute tile names, servant types or required numbers within already covered possession/count/threshold scoring rules. Nature and Domestic explicitly cover alternatives; upgrade independence and objective count are already tested.

candidate_rejections.candidate: Separate questions for ordinary cash/reputation activities such as Cricket Field, Billiards Room, Music Room, Drawing Room or Smoking Room.
candidate_rejections.reason: Their remaining distinctions are printed service, attendee and favour recipes. They add no new timing, exception or outcome branch beyond exact requirements, favours, mandatory upgrade and scoring.

candidate_rejections.candidate: May one ordinary servant cover multiple service icons or be moved from Servants’ Hall to the current activity?
candidate_rejections.reason: This makes explicit the normal requirement to provide a distinct available servant at each icon. Q02’s service step, Q08’s substitution conditions, Q19’s expended Hall servant and Q59’s requirement to fulfill all service needs already test this rule family. A new numerical double-assignment scenario would be a mechanical recombination. It would be reasonable to expand Q02’s key phrase to say one available servant per icon, but that is answer precision rather than a new procedural branch.

candidate_rejections.candidate: May an ordinary guest invite be refused or an unscreened bad draw returned without dismissal?
candidate_rejections.reason: Q37 already requires drawing, revealing and adding an ordinary invite to hand, distinguishes screening, and specifies rejected-card destinations. Q38 separately covers the optional dismissal route. Restating mandatory acquisition would not add a distinct outcome branch. Q02’s key could explicitly repeat that nonoptional favours must be taken, without needing a new question.

candidate_rejections.candidate: Does an acquired guest or purchased improvement above reputation still score?
candidate_rejections.reason: PR restriction is already tested as a play-only restriction, while Q15 scores all owned tiles and gentry. Combining those answers creates no new exception.

candidate_rejections.candidate: Can newly drawn or refreshed gentry attend the current activity?
candidate_rejections.reason: The ordered host sequence distinguishes draws during Enjoy Favours from preactivity VP-card use. Q50 explicitly tests immediate use of a recovered card; Q17 already allows VP-card use on the owner’s turn. Other examples would mechanically recombine established timing.

candidate_rejections.candidate: Can Servants’ Hall be activated when passing, or does a newly purchased monument pay retroactively?
candidate_rejections.reason: Q19 expressly tests Hall/monument timing on both turn choices. Q02 and Q03 place buying after the ongoing-effect check. These are covered consequences of the existing sequence.

candidate_rejections.candidate: Ask about additional reputation-overflow special actions, low-reputation gossip examples or exact-floor spending examples.
candidate_rejections.reason: The key already distinguishes costs, floor immunity, targeting restrictions, fixed screening reputation and spending during favours. More numeric cases do not introduce a new branch.

candidate_rejections.candidate: Ask whether the last bought tile or final special-action reputation loss affects final courtship or objectives.
candidate_rejections.reason: Current tableau/category scoring, final-courtship timing, postcourtship special actions and end-game objective possession are already independently specified. Combining them is not a new rule.

candidate_rejections.candidate: Socialite/antisocialite suite redraws, service-reduction combos, Business Room money and alternate West Terrace ongoing dismissal.
candidate_rejections.reason: These are marked expansion or alternate content. The base suite count restriction is already covered without importing expansion interactions. Corrigendum does not bring expansion content into base scope.

nonblocking_key_precision.question: Q02
nonblocking_key_precision.suggestion: If the key is edited for clarity, provide service could say one available matching/substituting servant per service icon, and enjoy favours could say all nonoptional favours. These are clarifications of the existing step, not new questions or detected contradictions.
